James Joyce was an Irish writer, born in Dublin in 1882, whose novel Ulysses changed the modern novel.

He left Ireland in 1904 and lived in Trieste, Zurich and Paris, but wrote almost only about Dublin. Dubliners, his stories, and A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man came first. Ulysses, published in Paris in 1922, follows a few Dubliners through a single day, 16 June 1904, using stream of consciousness and a different style in each chapter. It was banned for obscenity in the United States until 1933.

His last book, Finnegans Wake, pushed language further still. Joyce is a giant of modernism, with Yeats and Beckett one of the Irish writers who made Dublin a literary capital. Each 16 June readers celebrate Bloomsday. See Ireland.
sum: James Joyce was an Irish writer, born in Dublin in 1882, whose novel Ulysses changed the modern novel.
